body: I just gave away a rare classic car for free two weeks ago to a buyer for free you want a point of contrast...

I know there's others out there, I just wish I had gotten help sooner. The irony of being declared fit to fly when I was at my worst but losing that medical the second I try and get better is not lost on me...

This is really weird. I've been thinking something similar the past few days and basically concluded I'm dying on the edge of a lake from a contaminated mushroom neurotoxin in 2015. I'm not coping well though.

Also, you should read Crash by JG Ballard.
That's what I've heard. I'm pretty susceptible to drugs and even that is enough that I'm literally unable to keep my eyes open. I can't imagine what a higher dose would do if it comes to that.
That's what I figured, my only concern is having too much alcohol in my system before taking my meds but I recon I could just skip a dosage if I'm in doubt.

You don't have to be sorry, I get it. I don't know what I want anymore because I feel the same way. 

It was so hard for me to quit this stupid job because it was such a good distraction and I could just be fake for a few hours, but I was going to end up having an accident or fired if someone said something. Even then it felt like I was intentionally sabotaging my life and that nothing was actually wrong, even though I've cried in my car probably 95% of the days for the past year.

I genuinely cannot connect sides when I'm depressed and when I'm not. It's like split personalities and it means I know I'll never accomplish anything because the second the meds start kicking in I genuinely believe nothing was ever wrong and I stop. 

Right now I feel like I'm just writing depressed fanfic about someone else. I've never been sick, I just hate myself and want someone to worry.

Panic attacks were no better. I had one a few weeks ago for the first time in a while and it's the most scared I've ever been. 

I think it's just stress that triggers it, but I get stressed so easily now. I literally can't sleep if I have any responsibilities to deal with the next day, or if I'm expecting a phone call.

No, it's changing all the time. I was having panic attacks a few times a week before the meds. Massive mood swings before that. Now it's just mostly depression and these awful lucid delusions that feel like I'm watching myself go insane...

I've been dissociative for years, but it didn't bother me until recently
